summary: The frozen refinement keeps every public learning link and the optional local progress model. The corrupt-storage path persistence issue and the related stale history closure were repaired and independently reproduced successfully.
reviewedScope: Code and regression tests for selected-path curated next/resume, completed-step practice and final path choice.
Back/Forward selection, saved active-path persistence after repaired storage, same-path native practice/library hash navigation, modifier-link behavior.
Native path and full-library disclosures, server-rendered catalogue and no-JavaScript fallback sections. All 295 published guides plus nine tools remain represented.
Search over existing public titles, descriptions and jurisdictions only; query normalization and recoverable bookmark/started/no-match states.

Remembering remains off by default. Opt-in saves public identifiers and activity only. Reset/export and catalogue-failure protection retain the existing schema. No exercise or legal-source content was authored in this refinement.

findings.problem: With corrupt saved JSON and an explicit people path, opt-in previously saved the fallback model path. The ready-only history callback also retained the original storage error after repair.
findings.resolution: Opt-in first synchronizes the visible active path. A current-session ref supplies live storage error and saved path to the stable history callback.
findings.verified: One-time corrupt seed → people → opt-in saves people → choose economics saves economics → Back saves people → bare /learn/ restores people. Separate authored regression also covers a blocked write and recovery.

findings.boundary: With JavaScript enabled, a hand-written /learn/#learning-path-people fragment alone does not select the people path. App-generated links contain ?path=people plus a fragment; these work with JavaScript and target a real fallback section without it. Scope approval does not assert support for bare-fragment shorthand.
findings.reason: No app-generated link relies on the unsupported shorthand; the parent requested a narrow final change.
